title: New Sleeper Train Connects Tokyo to Aomori
paragraphs: Japan is getting a new overnight sleeper train. The train will connect Tokyo with Aomori, in the far north of Honshu, Japan's main island.

The train is called the Luna Azul, and it will be run by the railway company JR East. In June 2026, JR East announced that the train will start running in spring 2027. Some people say it is the first major new sleeper train in Japan since the Sunrise Express started in 1998.

The train will run two round trips a week. It will leave from Shinagawa Station in Tokyo at 9 p.m. and arrive at Aomori Station at 9 a.m. the next morning. At night, it will stop at stations such as Tokyo, Ueno and Omiya. In the morning, it will stop at Akita, Hirosaki and Shin-Aomori. On the way back, it will leave Aomori at 4 p.m. and arrive in Tokyo at 7 a.m. the next day. However, these times may change.

The train will have 10 cars. Nine of them will have private rooms for one person, two people or families. The tenth car will be a lounge with big windows. Up to 125 passengers can travel on the train.

In winter, there is a lot of snow in northern Japan, and fewer people travel there. So, in winter, the train will not go to Aomori. Instead, it will run during the day from Tokyo to Gunma Prefecture, near Kusatsu, a famous hot spring town.
JR East has not announced ticket prices yet. But it says that the prices will probably be higher than those for similar seats on the Tohoku Shinkansen.
